title: Exterior and interior renderings showing Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing and Hui Oi Chow Science Building signage and internal red stair feature
objects_and_counts: Top exterior region: a glass entrance facade with visible signage and at least 8 human silhouettes distributed across the forecourt and just inside the glass; several of these silhouettes are partially cropped or shown as semi-transparent render figures.
Top exterior region: brick building exterior behind the glass facade; planted shrubs and a low planting bed visible at right.

Lower-left interior panel: one prominent red perforated vertical/diagonal architectural stair enclosure and an adjacent stair, one illuminated wall sign reading 'FACULTY OF ENGINEERING' (neon-like), and at least 2 human render figures (one standing near the stair and one at upper level).

Lower-center interior panel: one red suspended stair element/structure, one open stair with black treads, at least 4 human render figures (two near the lower landing, two on the upper level), and a wall with a repeated dot-pattern mesh surface.

Lower-right interior panel: an open teaching/lounge area with multiple chairs and seating: at least 4 seated people visible, at least 4 round ottomans or low stools, and a bank of computer monitors and desks along the rear wall (the exact monitor count is not determinable from the image crop).

Repeated objects: the red architectural element (appearing at least in the three lower panels as a design motif), multiple glass doors/entrances in the top exterior region, and multiple ceiling light ribbons in the lower panels.
spatial_relations: Top exterior region: the 'Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing' sign is mounted on the glass canopy immediately above the main entrance; to the right of that entrance, 'HUI OI CHOW SCIENCE BUILDING' is mounted on the brick facade above another glass entrance.

Top exterior region: glass doors and transparent wall sections form a continuous glazed frontage below the signage; pedestrian silhouettes are distributed along a paved plaza directly in front of the glazed entrance.

Lower-left panel: the red perforated stair enclosure rises from a lower floor to an upper level, with the stair treads extending from left foreground to the upper right of that panel; the 'FACULTY OF ENGINEERING' illuminated sign is on the vertical surface to the left of the red element.

Lower-center panel: the open black-tread stair ascends beneath a suspended red rectangular stair volume; people stand on the landing area beneath and adjacent to a dotted-pattern wall (where 'TEACHINGSTUDIO' is visible).

Lower-right panel: the seating/lounge area occupies the foreground and midground with clustered seating (round ottomans and bench seating) and a row of desks/computers along the rear wall; people are seated on the floor and on raised bench seating at right.
colours_and_materials: Exterior: red-brown brick facade above a largely glass and metal framed ground-floor frontage; the paved plaza in front is an orange-brown brick or tile.
Interior: striking red painted or coated metal perforated stair enclosure and suspended red stair volume used as an accent in the lower panels.
Interior finishes: grey patterned carpet or floor tiles in lower panels, white ceilings with linear light elements, and glass partitions in several locations.
Furnishings: dark or black stair treads in the lower panels and neutral-coloured seating (grey and muted tones) in the lounge/teaching area.
uncertainties: The vertical Chinese text to the right of 'HUI OI CHOW SCIENCE BUILDING' on the brick facade is not fully legible in the image; transcription omitted for that line.

Counts of small repeated items (individual computer monitors, exact number of chairs/desks) cannot be precisely determined from the image crop and overlapping elements; only minimum visible counts are reported where reliable.
The lower-center wall text appears as 'TEACHINGSTUDIO' without a visible space; the exact spacing or punctuation as intended in the original cannot be confirmed from this image.
Some human figures are semi-transparent render silhouettes or partially cropped; exact counts of distinct people are minimum visible integers rather than a definitive room population.
Material identifications (for example, whether red elements are metal mesh or perforated metal) are visually inferred from appearance but not confirmed by any visible label.
